Medicine 10.question: ১) Which type of anemia is most common?
Medicine 10.exp:
Iron deficiency anemia (IDA) is the most common type of anemia worldwide. It occurs due to inadequate iron availability for hemoglobin synthesis, leading to microcytic hypochromic anemia. Common causes include chronic blood loss (especially menstrual loss and gastrointestinal bleeding), increased demand (pregnancy), and poor dietary intake.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common anemia → Iron deficiency anemia

  • Type: Microcytic hypochromic anemia

  • Blood findings:

    • ↓ Serum iron

    • ↓ Ferritin

    • ↑ Total iron-binding capacity (TIBC)

  • Common cause: Chronic blood loss

Exam Pearl:
The commonest anemia = Iron deficiency anemia (IDA).

Medicine 10.question: ২) Which is not a feature of inflammatory LBP?
Medicine 10.exp:
In inflammatory low back pain (LBP), pain typically improves with activity/exercise and worsens with rest, unlike mechanical back pain. Therefore, pain reducing on rest is NOT a feature of inflammatory LBP.

Features of inflammatory LBP:

  • Insidious onset

  • Morning stiffness (usually >30 minutes)

  • Improvement with exercise

  • Night pain (especially early morning)

  • May have systemic features (e.g., fatigue, associated inflammatory disease)

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Inflammatory LBP → better with movement, worse with rest

  • Mechanical LBP → better with rest, worse with activity

Exam Pearl:
Pain relieved by rest suggests mechanical, not inflammatory, low back pain.

Medicine 10.question: ৩) Which is not true about electrolyte imbalance in stored blood?
Medicine 10.exp:
Stored blood undergoes several biochemical changes during storage. Common electrolyte and metabolic abnormalities include:

  • Hyperkalemia → due to leakage of potassium from stored RBCs

  • Hypernatremia → may occur due to storage-related changes

  • Metabolic acidosis → due to accumulation of acidic metabolites (e.g., lactate)

Hypercalcemia is NOT a typical electrolyte imbalance in stored blood. In fact, stored blood may have low ionized calcium due to citrate anticoagulant binding calcium.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Stored blood changes:

    • ↑ Potassium

    • ↓ pH → metabolic acidosis

    • ↓ 2,3-DPG

    • ↓ ATP

    • Citrate binds calcium → risk of hypocalcemia during massive transfusion

Exam Pearl:
Stored blood → hyperkalemia, not hypercalcemia.

Medicine 10.question: ৪) How many histological subtypes of classical Hodgkin's lymphoma are there?
Medicine 10.exp:
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) has four histological subtypes:

  1. Nodular sclerosis type (most common)

  2. Mixed cellularity type

  3. Lymphocyte-rich type

  4. Lymphocyte-depleted type

(There is also nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, but it is classified separately and is not a subtype of classical Hodgkin lymphoma.)

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Classical Hodgkin lymphoma → 4 subtypes

  • Diagnostic cell: Reed–Sternberg cell

  • Most common subtype: Nodular sclerosis

  • RS cells express: CD15 and CD30

Exam Pearl:
Classical Hodgkin lymphoma has 4 histological subtypes.

Medicine 10.question: ৫) Which is most common type of arthritis in world?
Medicine 10.exp:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common type of arthritis worldwide. It is a degenerative joint disease caused by progressive loss of articular cartilage, subchondral bone changes, and osteophyte formation. It commonly affects weight-bearing joints such as the knees, hips, and spine, as well as the hands.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common arthritis → Osteoarthritis

  • Nature: Degenerative (non-inflammatory) arthritis

  • Common sites:

    • Knee

    • Hip

    • Spine

    • DIP/PIP joints of fingers

  • Risk factors:

    • Age

    • Obesity

    • Joint injury

Exam Pearl:
Commonest arthritis in the world = Osteoarthritis (OA).

Medicine 10.question: ৬) Which leukemia is common in children?
Medicine 10.exp:
Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is the most common leukemia in children, especially between 2–5 years of age. It arises from malignant proliferation of lymphoid precursor cells, most commonly B-cell lineage.

Other options:

  • AML → more common in adults than children

  • CML → uncommon in children

  • CLL → primarily a disease of older adults and rare in children

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common childhood leukemia → ALL

  • Peak age → 2–5 years

  • Common type → B-cell ALL

  • Diagnosis → Bone marrow examination showing increased lymphoblasts

Exam Pearl:
Child + leukemia = think ALL.

Medicine 10.question: ৭) Which is a hallmark of osteoarthritis?
Medicine 10.exp:
Osteophyte formation is a hallmark feature of osteoarthritis (OA). Osteophytes are bony outgrowths that develop at joint margins due to degenerative changes and are a characteristic finding on X-ray.

Other options:

  • Syndesmophyte formation → characteristic of ankylosing spondylitis

  • Muscle weakness → may occur but is not the hallmark

  • Restriction of movement → can occur in OA but is not the defining feature

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Osteoarthritis → Osteophytes + joint space narrowing

  • Degenerative arthritis (non-inflammatory)

  • Commonly affects:

    • Knee

    • Hip

    • Spine

    • DIP/PIP joints

Exam Pearl:
Osteophytes are the classic hallmark of osteoarthritis.

Medicine 10.question: ৮) Which is the single best test to confirm iron deficiency?
Medicine 10.exp:
Serum (plasma) ferritin is the single best test to confirm iron deficiency because it reflects the body's iron stores. A low ferritin level is highly specific for iron deficiency anemia.

Other tests:

  • Plasma iron → decreased in iron deficiency but varies widely and is less reliable.

  • TIBC → increased in iron deficiency, but not confirmatory alone.

  • Transferrin → may increase, but less specific than ferritin.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Iron deficiency anemia:

    • ↓ Ferritin (best indicator)

    • ↓ Serum iron

    • ↑ TIBC

    • ↓ Transferrin saturation

    • Microcytic hypochromic RBCs

Exam Pearl:
Best confirmatory test for iron deficiency = Low serum ferritin.

Medicine 10.question: ৯) According to ARA criteria which is minimum score required for diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis?
Medicine 10.exp:
According to the ACR/EULAR (American Rheumatism Association) criteria for rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a minimum score of 6 out of 10 is required for classification as rheumatoid arthritis (provided synovitis is present and no better alternative diagnosis exists).

The scoring system includes:

  • Joint involvement → 0–5 points

  • Serology (RF, anti-CCP) → 0–3 points

  • Acute phase reactants (ESR, CRP) → 0–1 point

  • Duration of symptoms ≥6 weeks → 0–1 point

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • RA diagnosis/classification → ≥6/10 points

  • Key antibody: Anti-CCP

  • Classic features:

    • Symmetrical small joint arthritis

    • Morning stiffness

    • Rheumatoid nodules

Exam Pearl:
ACR/EULAR criteria for RA = minimum score 6.

Medicine 10.question: ১০) Which investigation is done to see prognosis of Hodgkin's lymphoma?
Medicine 10.exp:
In Hodgkin's lymphoma, ESR is an important prognostic indicator. A raised ESR is associated with higher disease activity and poorer prognosis, especially in early-stage disease.

Other options:

  • LDH → more commonly used as a prognostic marker in non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

  • PBF (Peripheral blood film) → helps assess blood abnormalities but is not a main prognostic marker.

  • CXR → used for staging (e.g., mediastinal involvement), not primarily for prognosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hodgkin lymphoma prognosis → ESR

  • Non-Hodgkin lymphoma prognosis → LDH

  • Hodgkin lymphoma hallmark: Reed–Sternberg cells

  • Common subtype: Nodular sclerosis

Exam Pearl:
Raised ESR indicates poorer prognosis in Hodgkin lymphoma.

Medicine 10.question: ১১) Which is not an indication of fresh frozen plasma?
Medicine 10.exp:
Fresh frozen plasma (FFP) contains clotting factors and is indicated for conditions with deficiency of coagulation factors, such as:

  • DIC (Disseminated intravascular coagulation) ✅

  • Hemophilia (when specific factor concentrates are unavailable) ✅

  • Clotting factor disorders ✅

ITP is a disorder of platelet destruction causing thrombocytopenia, not a clotting factor deficiency. Therefore, FFP is not indicated for ITP.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • FFP → replaces clotting factors

  • Indications:

    • DIC

    • Liver disease with coagulopathy

    • Massive transfusion with factor deficiency

    • Hemophilia (if factor concentrate unavailable)

  • ITP → platelet problem → treat with steroids/IVIG/platelets in selected cases

Exam Pearl:
FFP is not used for ITP because ITP is a platelet disorder, not a coagulation factor deficiency.

Medicine 10.question: ১২) Which investigation is done for confirmation of acute leukemia?
Medicine 10.exp:
Bone marrow examination is the confirmatory investigation for acute leukemia. It demonstrates increased blast cells in the marrow and helps classify the type of leukemia (ALL, AML, etc.) using morphology, cytochemistry, immunophenotyping, and cytogenetic studies.

Other options:

  • PBF (Peripheral blood film) → may suggest leukemia by showing blasts, but not confirmatory.

  • CBC → shows abnormalities like anemia, leukocytosis/leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, but not diagnostic.

  • Chromosomal study → helps classification and prognosis after diagnosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute leukemia confirmation → Bone marrow aspiration/biopsy

  • Diagnostic criterion: ≥20% blasts in bone marrow (for most acute leukemias)

  • Further classification:

    • Flow cytometry

    • Cytogenetics

Exam Pearl:
Confirm acute leukemia = Bone marrow study.

Medicine 10.question: ১৩) Deformities in rheumatoid arthritis excludes....?
Medicine 10.exp:
Radial deviation is not a typical deformity of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). RA commonly causes deformities due to chronic synovitis and tendon damage, especially in the hands.

Common RA deformities include:

  • ✅ Swan neck deformity (hyperextension of PIP with flexion of DIP)

  • ✅ Boutonniere deformity (flexion of PIP with hyperextension of DIP)

  • ✅ Z-thumb deformity (Z deformity of thumb)

  • ✅ Ulnar deviation of fingers (classic RA feature)

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • RA hand deformity → Ulnar deviation

  • Swan neck → RA

  • Boutonniere → RA

  • Z-thumb → RA

  • Radial deviation → not typical

Exam Pearl:
Deformity excluded in rheumatoid arthritis = Radial deviation.

Medicine 10.question: ১৪) A transferrin saturation of less than...... is consistent with iron deficiency?
Medicine 10.exp:
A transferrin saturation (TSAT) of less than 16% is consistent with iron deficiency. Transferrin saturation reflects the amount of iron available for hemoglobin synthesis.

Typical iron deficiency anemia profile:

  • ↓ Serum ferritin

  • ↓ Serum iron

  • ↑ TIBC

  • ↓ Transferrin saturation (<16%)

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Iron deficiency → TSAT <16%

  • Ferritin → best indicator of iron stores

  • Morphology → microcytic hypochromic anemia

Exam Pearl:
Transferrin saturation <16% = iron deficiency anemia.

Medicine 10.question: ১৫) Which is a feature of Non Hodgkin's lymphoma?
Medicine 10.exp:
Leukemic transformation is a feature more commonly associated with Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), where malignant lymphoid cells may spill into the blood and resemble leukemia.

Other options:

  • RS cell (Reed–Sternberg cell) → characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma, not NHL.

  • Itching (pruritus) → classically associated with Hodgkin lymphoma.

  • Pel–Ebstein fever → characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma (though uncommon).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hodgkin lymphoma → RS cells + Pel–Ebstein fever + pruritus

  • Non-Hodgkin lymphoma → extranodal involvement + leukemic transformation possible

Exam Pearl:
Feature of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma among the options = Leukemic transformation.

Medicine 10.question: ১৬) Anti TNF therapy used in RA excludes....?
Medicine 10.exp:
Rituximab is not an anti-TNF therapy. It is a B-cell–depleting monoclonal antibody that targets CD20 on B lymphocytes and is used in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), especially in patients who fail TNF inhibitors.

Anti-TNF drugs used in RA include:

  • ✅ Etanercept

  • ✅ Infliximab

  • ✅ Adalimumab

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Anti-TNF agents:

    • Etanercept (TNF receptor fusion protein)

    • Infliximab (anti-TNF monoclonal antibody)

    • Adalimumab (anti-TNF monoclonal antibody)

  • Rituximab → Anti-CD20 B-cell therapy

Exam Pearl:
Anti-TNF therapy excludes = Rituximab.

Medicine 10.question: ১৭) In acute leukemia blast cell is at least more than.......?
Medicine 10.exp:
In acute leukemia, the diagnosis is made when blast cells are ≥20% in the bone marrow (according to WHO criteria, with some genetic exceptions).

Options:

  • 20%  → Diagnostic cutoff

  • 30%, 40%, 50%  → Not the standard diagnostic threshold

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute leukemia → Bone marrow blasts ≥20%

  • Confirmatory test → Bone marrow study

  • Further classification → Flow cytometry & cytogenetics

Exam Pearl:
Acute leukemia = ≥20% blasts in bone marrow.

Medicine 10.question: ১৮) Which investigation is done to monitor disease damage caused by RA?
Medicine 10.exp:
X-ray is used to monitor structural joint damage and disease progression in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). It can show:

  • Joint space narrowing

  • Marginal erosions

  • Bone destruction

  • Deformities

Other options:

  • ESR & CRP → monitor inflammatory activity and response to treatment, not actual joint damage.

  • ACPA (anti-CCP antibody) → diagnostic and prognostic marker, not for monitoring damage.

  • Urinalysis → not used for RA damage assessment.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • RA activity → ESR, CRP

  • RA diagnosis → RF, anti-CCP (ACPA)

  • RA joint damage → X-ray

Exam Pearl:
Investigation to monitor RA disease damage = X-ray.

Medicine 10.question: ১৯) Anemia associated with which condition may not require blood transfusion?
Medicine 10.exp:
In patients with anemia associated with heart failure, blood transfusion may not always be required because transfusion can increase circulatory volume and potentially worsen cardiac failure (risk of fluid overload). Management depends on severity and clinical condition.

Other options:

  • Angina → anemia may worsen myocardial ischemia; transfusion may be considered in severe cases.

  • Bleeding tendency → transfusion may be needed depending on blood loss and severity.

  • Cerebral hypoxia → severe anemia causing reduced oxygen delivery may require correction, including transfusion in selected cases.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Transfusion decision depends on:

    • Hemoglobin level

    • Symptoms

    • Rate of blood loss

    • Comorbidities

  • Avoid unnecessary transfusion in heart failure due to risk of volume overload.

Exam Pearl:
Anemia with heart failure may not require

Medicine 10.question: ২০) 1 bag platelet concentrate is prepared from...... bags of fresh blood?
Medicine 10.exp:
1 bag of platelet concentrate is prepared from approximately 4 bags of fresh whole blood (depending on preparation method and blood service standards).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Platelet concentrate → pooled from multiple donor units

  • Common exam value:

    • 1 adult therapeutic platelet dose ≈ 4–6 random donor platelet units

  • Apheresis platelets → collected from a single donor

Exam Pearl:
1 bag platelet concentrate = prepared from 4 bags of fresh blood.

Medicine 10.question: ২১) Diagnostic criteria of multiple myeloma excludes......?
Medicine 10.option1: increased malignant plasma cells in bone marrow
Medicine 10.exp:
Bony tenderness is not a diagnostic criterion for multiple myeloma. The diagnosis is based on evidence of malignant plasma cell proliferation and end-organ damage.

Diagnostic features include:

  •  Increased malignant plasma cells in bone marrow (≥10% or plasmacytoma)

  •  Serum/urinary M protein (monoclonal protein)

  •  Skeletal lytic lesions

Common CRAB features of multiple myeloma:

  • C → Hypercalcemia

  • R → Renal impairment

  • A → Anemia

  • B → Bone lesions (lytic lesions)

Exam Pearl:
Multiple myeloma diagnostic criteria excludes = Bony tenderness.

Medicine 10.question: ২২) Which is not a phase of specific therapy in acute leukemia?
Medicine 10.exp:
Specific therapy of acute leukemia is classically divided into three major phases: remission induction, remission consolidation (intensification), and remission maintenance (especially important in acute lymphoblastic leukemia). Remission induction aims to achieve complete remission by eliminating detectable leukemic cells. Consolidation therapy eradicates residual disease and reduces relapse risk. Maintenance therapy uses prolonged lower-intensity treatment to maintain remission. Remission termination is not a recognized phase of leukemia-specific therapy. It is not part of standard leukemia treatment protocols and is therefore the incorrect option.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Induction therapy: Achieves complete remission.

  • Consolidation/intensification therapy: Eliminates minimal residual disease.

  • Maintenance therapy: Prevents relapse, especially in ALL.

  • AML usually requires induction and consolidation; routine maintenance is less commonly used.

Exam Pearl:
The standard phases of acute leukemia therapy are induction → consolidation → maintenance; remission termination is not a treatment phase.

Medicine 10.question: ২৩) Which type of anemia is common in hospital population?
Medicine 10.exp:
The most common type of anemia encountered among hospitalized patients is anemia of chronic disease (ACD), also known as anemia of inflammation. It occurs due to underlying chronic infections, inflammatory disorders, malignancies, and chronic organ diseases. Inflammatory cytokines, especially IL-6, increase hepatic production of hepcidin, which inhibits iron release from macrophages and decreases intestinal iron absorption. This leads to reduced availability of iron for erythropoiesis despite adequate or increased body iron stores. Iron deficiency anemia is common in the general population but is not the most common anemia specifically associated with hospitalized patients.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ACD: low serum iron, low TIBC, normal/increased ferritin.

  • Main mechanism: increased hepcidin causing iron trapping in macrophages.

  • Common causes: chronic infection, autoimmune disease, malignancy, chronic kidney disease.

  • Iron deficiency anemia: low ferritin and increased TIBC.

Exam Pearl:
In hospitalized patients, think anemia of chronic disease/inflammation due to increased hepcidin-mediated iron sequestration.

Medicine 10.question: ২৪) Philadelphia chromosomes is associated with which type of leukemia?
Medicine 10.exp:
The Philadelphia chromosome is classically associated with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It results from a reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22: t(9;22)(q34;q11). This creates the BCR-ABL fusion gene, which encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase. The uncontrolled signaling from this abnormal kinase promotes excessive proliferation of myeloid cells, leading to CML. The Philadelphia chromosome may also be seen in a subset of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (especially adult B-cell ALL), but the classic and most strongly associated disease is CML.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Philadelphia chromosome: t(9;22).

  • Fusion gene: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase.

  • Classical association: Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML).

  • BCR-ABL positive ALL can occur, especially in adults.

Exam Pearl:
Philadelphia chromosome = CML (BCR-ABL from t(9;22)).

Medicine 10.question: ২৫) Which is hallmark of hemophilia?
Medicine 10.exp:
The hallmark feature of hemophilia is hemarthrosis, which refers to bleeding into joints, especially large joints such as the knees, ankles, and elbows. Hemophilia is an inherited coagulation disorder caused by deficiency of clotting factors: factor VIII in hemophilia A and factor IX in hemophilia B. Since the defect involves secondary hemostasis, bleeding occurs in deep tissues, muscles, and joints rather than mucosal surfaces or skin. Gum bleeding and purpuric spots are more typical of platelet disorders, while anemia may occur secondary to chronic blood loss but is not a defining feature.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hemophilia: X-linked recessive disorder.

  • Hemophilia A: factor VIII deficiency.

  • Hemophilia B: factor IX deficiency.

  • Laboratory finding: prolonged aPTT with normal PT.

  • Typical bleeding: deep tissue bleeding and hemarthrosis.

Exam Pearl:
Hemarthrosis is the classic bleeding manifestation of hemophilia due to a coagulation factor defect.

Medicine 10.question: ২৬) Typical ‘bamboo spine’ sign in X-ray signifies....?
Medicine 10.exp:
The bamboo spine appearance on X-ray is a characteristic finding of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). It occurs due to chronic inflammation at the entheses, particularly affecting the sacroiliac joints and spinal ligaments. Progressive formation of marginal syndesmophytes bridges adjacent vertebral bodies, producing a continuous, fused appearance resembling bamboo. AS is a seronegative spondyloarthropathy strongly associated with HLA-B27. Rheumatoid arthritis primarily affects peripheral joints and may cause atlantoaxial subluxation but does not produce a bamboo spine. Osteoarthritis produces degenerative osteophytes, while SLE mainly causes non-erosive arthritis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bamboo spine: ankylosing spondylitis.

  • Key X-ray finding: marginal syndesmophytes.

  • Early radiological sign: sacroiliitis.

  • Association: HLA-B27.

  • Part of seronegative spondyloarthropathies.

Exam Pearl:
Bamboo spine = ankylosing spondylitis due to bridging syndesmophytes.

Medicine 10.question: ২৭) Which vitamin deficiency causes anemia with neurological symptoms?
Medicine 10.exp:
Vitamin B12 deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia with neurological manifestations. Vitamin B12 is required for DNA synthesis and for the maintenance of normal myelin formation. Deficiency leads to impaired DNA synthesis, causing ineffective erythropoiesis and macrocytic anemia. Neurological features occur due to defective myelin production and include peripheral neuropathy, paresthesia, loss of vibration and position sense, and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord. Folate deficiency also causes megaloblastic anemia but does not cause neurological symptoms. Vitamin B6 deficiency may cause sideroblastic anemia, while vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy-related bleeding and impaired wound healing.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Vitamin B12 deficiency: megaloblastic anemia + neurological symptoms.

  • Neurological complication: subacute combined degeneration.

  • Common causes: pernicious anemia, malabsorption, strict vegan diet.

  • Folate deficiency: megaloblastic anemia without neurological signs.

  • B12 and folate deficiency: increased homocysteine.

Exam Pearl:
B12 deficiency = megaloblastic anemia with neurological involvement; folate deficiency lacks neurological features.

Medicine 10.question: ২৮) Which is most common variety of leukemia?
Medicine 10.exp:
The most common variety of leukemia overall is chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), particularly among adults in Western populations. CLL is a neoplastic disorder of mature but functionally ineffective B lymphocytes, characterized by progressive accumulation of these cells in blood, bone marrow, lymph nodes, and spleen. However, the most common leukemia in children is acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Since the question asks generally for the most common variety of leukemia without specifying age group, CLL is considered the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common leukemia overall: CLL.

  • Most common childhood leukemia: ALL.

  • CLL is a malignancy of mature B cells.

  • AML is the most common acute leukemia in adults.

  • CML is associated with BCR-ABL (Philadelphia chromosome).

Exam Pearl:
CLL = most common leukemia overall; ALL = most common leukemia in children.

Medicine 10.question: ২৯) Which drug is used in 1st line treatment of multiple myeloma?
Medicine 10.exp:
Bortezomib, a proteasome inhibitor, is one of the key first-line drugs used in the treatment of multiple myeloma. It inhibits the 26S proteasome, causing accumulation of abnormal proteins within plasma cells and leading to apoptosis. Modern initial therapy commonly includes combinations containing a proteasome inhibitor (such as bortezomib), an immunomodulatory drug, and corticosteroid. Melphalan was historically used, especially in older regimens, but is not the preferred first-line agent in current practice. Prednisolone is used as part of combination therapy but is not the main targeted drug. Imatinib is used for BCR-ABL–positive leukemias such as CML.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Multiple myeloma arises from malignant plasma cells.

  • Bortezomib: proteasome inhibitor; major first-line therapy.

  • Common combination: bortezomib + immunomodulator + corticosteroid.

  • Myeloma markers: M protein, lytic bone lesions, hypercalcemia, renal impairment, anemia.

  • Imatinib: associated with CML, not myeloma.

Exam Pearl:
Bortezomib is a cornerstone first-line therapy for multiple myeloma due to proteasome inhibition.

Medicine 10.question: ৩০) Where absorption of vit B12 occurs?
Medicine 10.exp:
Absorption of vitamin B12 (cobalamin) occurs mainly in the terminal ileum. Dietary vitamin B12 first binds with intrinsic factor, a glycoprotein secreted by gastric parietal cells. The vitamin B12–intrinsic factor complex then travels through the small intestine and binds to specific receptors in the terminal ileal mucosa, allowing absorption into the bloodstream. Defects affecting intrinsic factor production (e.g., pernicious anemia) or terminal ileal disease/resection (e.g., Crohn disease) can cause vitamin B12 deficiency. The duodenum and jejunum are mainly involved in other nutrient absorption, while the colon has no significant role in vitamin B12 absorption.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Site of vitamin B12 absorption: Terminal ileum

  • Required factor: Intrinsic factor from gastric parietal cells

  • Vitamin B12 deficiency causes: Megaloblastic anemia + neurological manifestations

  • Terminal ileum also absorbs: Bile salts

Exam Pearl:
Vitamin B12 absorption requires intrinsic factor a

Medicine 10.question: ৩১) Imatinib is usually used in which type of leukemia?
Medicine 10.exp:
Imatinib is a targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor primarily used in chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It specifically inhibits the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase, which is produced by the Philadelphia chromosome (t(9;22)) translocation. This abnormal fusion protein causes uncontrolled proliferation of myeloid cells in CML. Imatinib has dramatically improved the prognosis of CML and is considered first-line therapy in most patients. It may also be used in some cases of Philadelphia chromosome-positive ALL, but its classic and most commonly tested indication is CML. AML and CLL are not primarily treated with imatinib.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Imatinib target: BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase

  • Genetic abnormality in CML: Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)

  • Classic disease treated with imatinib: CML

  • Mechanism: Tyrosine kinase inhibition

Exam Pearl:
Imatinib is the prototype targeted therapy for Philadelphia chromosome-positive CML.

Medicine 10.question: ৩২) Which is not true about rheumatoid arthritis?
Medicine 10.exp:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by persistent, usually symmetrical polyarthritis affecting predominantly the small joints of the hands and feet, especially the metacarpophalangeal and proximal interphalangeal joints. The arthritis in RA is typically additive and persistent, not migratory. Migratory arthritis is classically associated with acute rheumatic fever, where inflammation moves from one joint to another. Therefore, migratory arthritis is not a typical feature of rheumatoid arthritis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • RA is an autoimmune inflammatory polyarthritis

  • Typical joints: MCP, PIP, wrist

  • RA usually causes symmetrical, non-migratory arthritis

  • DIP joints are usually spared in RA

  • Migratory arthritis → acute rheumatic fever

Exam Pearl:
Rheumatoid arthritis causes symmetrical small joint polyarthritis, but it is not migratory.

Medicine 10.question: ৩৩) Which is not one of the classical feature of thalassemia?
Medicine 10.exp:
The classical features of thalassemia result from chronic hemolytic anemia and ineffective erythropoiesis. Common findings include anemia, jaundice due to increased breakdown of red blood cells, and splenomegaly due to extramedullary hematopoiesis and increased sequestration of abnormal erythrocytes. In severe thalassemia, hepatomegaly can occur due to extramedullary hematopoiesis and iron overload from repeated blood transfusions, but it is not considered one of the classical hallmark features. Therefore, among the given options, hepatomegaly is the least typical classical feature.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thalassemia causes microcytic hypochromic anemia

  • Chronic hemolysis → jaundice

  • Increased extramedullary hematopoiesis → splenomegaly

  • Severe cases may develop bone deformities and iron overload

Exam Pearl:
The classical triad of thalassemia includes anemia, jaundice, and splenomegaly.

Medicine 10.question: ৩৪) Which is not a cause of vit B12 deficiency?
Medicine 10.exp:
Vitamin B12 deficiency occurs due to inadequate intake, impaired absorption, or problems affecting intrinsic factor production. Strict vegans are at risk because vitamin B12 is mainly found in animal-derived foods. Total gastrectomy causes deficiency because gastric parietal cells are removed, leading to loss of intrinsic factor required for B12 absorption. Small bowel pathology, especially involving the terminal ileum, can impair absorption of the vitamin B12–intrinsic factor complex. Hookworm infestation primarily causes iron deficiency anemia due to chronic intestinal blood loss and is not a recognized cause of vitamin B12 deficiency.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Vitamin B12 absorption site: Terminal ileum

  • Required for absorption: Intrinsic factor from gastric parietal cells

  • Total gastrectomy → loss of intrinsic factor → B12 deficiency

  • Hookworm → iron deficiency anemia

Exam Pearl:
Hookworm causes iron deficiency anemia, not vitamin B12 deficiency.

Medicine 10.question: ৩৫) A 70 years male presented with anemia, infection, painless lymphadenopathy with systemic symptoms. What is most likely diagnosis?
Medicine 10.exp:
A 70-year-old patient with anemia, recurrent infections, painless lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms most likely has chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). CLL is the most common leukemia in older adults and results from the clonal proliferation of mature but functionally ineffective B lymphocytes. Anemia occurs due to bone marrow infiltration or autoimmune hemolysis, while infections occur because abnormal lymphocytes impair normal immune function. Painless lymphadenopathy and constitutional symptoms such as fever, night sweats, and weight loss are common. AML and ALL are usually more acute in presentation, while CML typically presents with marked leukocytosis and splenomegaly.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CLL is the most common leukemia in elderly patients

  • Cell type: Mature B lymphocytes

  • Typical findings: Painless lymphadenopathy, anemia, recurrent infections

  • Peripheral smear: Smudge cells

  • CLL is associated with hypogammaglobulinemia

Exam Pearl:
Elderly patient + painless lymphadenopathy + recurrent infections = CLL.

Medicine 10.question: ৩৬) Which is used as 2nd line therapy in ITP?
Medicine 10.exp:
In immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), first-line treatment usually includes corticosteroids (prednisolone) and, in situations requiring rapid platelet increase, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). For patients with persistent or relapsed ITP who do not respond adequately to first-line therapy, splenectomy has traditionally been used as a second-line treatment because the spleen is the major site of platelet destruction and autoantibody production. Newer second-line options include thrombopoietin receptor agonists and rituximab, but among the given options, splenectomy is the accepted answer. Tacrolimus is not a standard therapy for ITP.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ITP = autoimmune destruction of platelets

  • First-line therapy: Corticosteroids

  • Rapid platelet rise: IVIG

  • Traditional second-line therapy: Splenectomy

  • Site of platelet destruction in ITP: Spleen

Exam Pearl:
Persistent ITP after steroid therapy → consider splenectomy as a classic second-line treatment.

Medicine 10.question: ৩৭) Which type of anemia is characterized by hypersegmented neutrophil in PBF?
Medicine 10.exp:
Hypersegmented neutrophils on peripheral blood film (PBF) are a classic morphological feature of megaloblastic anemia, which results from impaired DNA synthesis. The most common causes are vitamin B12 deficiency and folate deficiency. Due to defective DNA replication, nuclear maturation is delayed while cytoplasmic maturation continues, producing large abnormal cells including macro-ovalocytes and neutrophils with excessive nuclear lobulation (usually more than 5 lobes). Iron deficiency anemia typically shows microcytic hypochromic cells, while hemolytic anemia shows features such as reticulocytosis and schistocytes/spherocytes depending on the cause. Sideroblastic anemia may show ring sideroblasts in bone marrow.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypersegmented neutrophils → Megaloblastic anemia

  • Main causes: Vitamin B12 deficiency and folate deficiency

  • PBF finding: Macro-ovalocytes + hypersegmented neutrophils

  • B12 deficiency may cause neurological manifestations

  • Folate deficiency does not cause neurological deficits

Exam Pearl:
Hypersegmented neutrophils are the hallmark peripheral smear finding of megaloblastic anemia.

Medicine 10.question: ৩৮) A 25 year old male patient presented with bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain & purpuric spot in buttocks. what may be the possible diagnosis?
Medicine 10.exp:
A young adult presenting with bloody diarrhoea, abdominal pain, and purpuric spots on the buttocks is suggestive of Henoch–Schönlein purpura (HSP), also known as IgA vasculitis. HSP is an immune-mediated small vessel vasculitis characterized by deposition of IgA-containing immune complexes. The classic clinical features are palpable purpura (especially over lower limbs and buttocks), abdominal pain, arthritis/arthralgia, and renal involvement. Gastrointestinal involvement can cause abdominal pain and gastrointestinal bleeding. ITP causes isolated thrombocytopenia with purpura but does not typically cause abdominal symptoms or bloody diarrhoea.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HSP = IgA small vessel vasculitis

  • Classic tetrad: Purpura, abdominal pain, arthritis, renal involvement

  • Purpura distribution: Buttocks and lower limbs

  • Common renal finding: Hematuria

  • More common in children but can occur in adults

Exam Pearl:
Purpura + abdominal pain + GI bleeding = Think Henoch–Schönlein purpura (IgA vasculitis).

Medicine 10.question: ৩৯) In which leukemia splenomegaly is common?
Medicine 10.exp:
Splenomegaly is a very common and often prominent feature of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It occurs due to marked proliferation of myeloid cells and extramedullary hematopoiesis in the spleen. Patients with CML may present with massive splenomegaly, fatigue, weight loss, and symptoms related to increased white cell count. Although splenomegaly can occur in other leukemias such as ALL and CLL, it is classically associated with CML, where it may be a major clinical finding. AML usually presents more acutely with bone marrow failure features such as anemia, infection, and bleeding.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CML associated with massive splenomegaly

  • CML genetic marker: Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22)

  • Mechanism: Extramedullary hematopoiesis

  • CLL: lymphadenopathy + recurrent infections in elderly

  • AML: anemia, infection, bleeding due to marrow failure

Exam Pearl:
Massive splenomegaly in a leukemia patient strongly suggests CML.

Medicine 10.question: ৪০) Hallmarks of hemolysis excludes......?
Medicine 10.exp:
The hallmark laboratory features of hemolysis include increased unconjugated bilirubin, increased lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) due to red cell destruction, increased reticulocyte count due to compensatory bone marrow response, and decreased hemoglobin due to anemia. In hemolysis, breakdown of hemoglobin produces excess bilirubin, which is initially unconjugated (indirect). Conjugated bilirubin is typically increased in hepatobiliary disease or conditions causing impaired excretion of bilirubin. Therefore, increased conjugated bilirubin is not a typical marker of hemolysis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hemolysis markers:

    • ↑ Unconjugated bilirubin

    • ↑ LDH

    • ↑ Reticulocyte count

    • ↓ Haptoglobin

  • Intravascular hemolysis → marked LDH rise + low haptoglobin

  • Extravascular hemolysis → splenic RBC destruction

Exam Pearl:
Hemolysis causes increased indirect (unconjugated) bilirubin, not conjugated bilirubin.

Medicine 10.question: ৪১) Classical hemophilia occurs due to deficiency of which clotting factor?
Medicine 10.exp:
Classical hemophilia (Hemophilia A) occurs due to deficiency or dysfunction of clotting factor VIII. It is an X-linked recessive bleeding disorder that mainly affects males. Factor VIII is an essential component of the intrinsic coagulation pathway, and its deficiency leads to impaired clot formation. Patients typically present with deep tissue bleeding, including hemarthrosis, muscle hematomas, and prolonged bleeding after trauma or surgery. Hemophilia B is caused by factor IX deficiency and is also X-linked, but it is less common. Factor VII deficiency affects the extrinsic pathway, while factor X deficiency affects the common pathway.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hemophilia A = Factor VIII deficiency

  • Hemophilia B = Factor IX deficiency

  • Inheritance: X-linked recessive

  • Coagulation test: Prolonged aPTT with normal PT

  • Common bleeding site: Joints (hemarthrosis)

Exam Pearl:
Classical hemophilia = Hemophilia A = Factor VIII deficiency.

Medicine 10.question: ৪২) Which is a hallmark of Ankylosing spondylitis?
Medicine 10.exp:
The hallmark radiological feature of ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is syndesmophyte formation. AS is a chronic inflammatory spondyloarthropathy that primarily affects the sacroiliac joints and spine. Inflammation at the vertebral entheses leads to new bone formation along the outer fibers of the annulus fibrosus, producing thin vertical bony bridges between adjacent vertebral bodies called syndesmophytes. Over time, extensive syndesmophyte formation results in a characteristic “bamboo spine” appearance on X-ray. Osteophytes are more typical of degenerative osteoarthritis. Restriction of movement is a clinical feature of AS but is not the hallmark radiological finding.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • AS associated with HLA-B27

  • Main joints involved: Sacroiliac joints and spine

  • X-ray finding: Marginal syndesmophytes → bamboo spine

  • Age of onset: Usually young adults

  • Inflammatory back pain improves with exercise

Exam Pearl:
Syndesmophytes and bamboo spine are classic hallmarks of ankylosing spondylitis.

Medicine 10.question: ৪৩) Which is not true about osteoarthritis?
Medicine 10.exp:
Osteoarthritis (OA) is a chronic degenerative joint disease characterized by progressive loss of articular cartilage, subchondral bone changes, and osteophyte formation. It commonly affects weight-bearing joints such as the knee and hip, as well as the hands. Unlike rheumatoid arthritis, OA is not an autoimmune inflammatory disease and does not show ACPA (anti-citrullinated protein antibody) positivity. ACPA is a highly specific marker associated with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Therefore, ACPA positivity is not a feature of osteoarthritis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • OA = Degenerative joint disease

  • Common joints: Knee, hip, spine, DIP, PIP

  • X-ray findings: Joint space narrowing + osteophyte formation

  • ACPA positivity → Rheumatoid arthritis

  • OA pain worsens with activity and improves with rest

Exam Pearl:
ACPA positivity suggests rheumatoid arthritis, not osteoarthritis.

Medicine 10.question: ৪৪) Which DMARD causes irreversible ototoxicity & retinopathy?
Medicine 10.exp:
Hydroxychloroquine is a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) used mainly in rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus. Its most important adverse effect is retinopathy, which can be irreversible and may lead to visual impairment if not detected early. Long-term use requires regular ophthalmological screening. Hydroxychloroquine can also rarely cause ototoxicity, including hearing impairment. Methotrexate is associated with hepatotoxicity and bone marrow suppression, sulfasalazine may cause hypersensitivity and cytopenias, and leflunomide commonly causes hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hydroxychloroquine adverse effect: Retinopathy

  • Requires regular eye screening during long-term therapy

  • Used in: Rheumatoid arthritis and SLE

  • Methotrexate → hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression

  • Leflunomide → hepatotoxicity, teratogenicity

Exam Pearl:
Hydroxychloroquine = irreversible retinal toxicity (retinopathy) requiring eye monitoring.

Medicine 10.question: ৪৫) Seronegative spondyloarthritis excludes....?
Medicine 10.exp:
Seronegative spondyloarthritis (SpA) refers to a group of inflammatory arthritic disorders characterized by negative rheumatoid factor (RF) and involvement of the axial skeleton, entheses, and sacroiliac joints. The major diseases included are ankylosing spondylitis, reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, enteropathic arthritis, and undifferentiated SpA. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a separate autoimmune inflammatory arthritis that is typically associated with positive RF and ACPA, although some patients may be seronegative. RA primarily affects peripheral joints and does not belong to the spondyloarthritis group.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Seronegative SpA → usually RF negative

  • Associated with HLA-B27

  • Includes:

    • Ankylosing spondylitis

    • Reactive arthritis

    • Psoriatic arthritis

    • Enteropathic arthritis

  • RA → ACPA/RF-associated autoimmune arthritis

Exam Pearl:
Ankylosing spondylitis, reactive arthritis, and psoriatic arthritis are SpA; rheumatoid arthritis is not.

Medicine 10.question: ৪৬) HLA B27 is associated with which disease?
Medicine 10.exp:
HLA-B27 is strongly associated with ankylosing spondylitis (AS), a chronic inflammatory seronegative spondyloarthritis affecting mainly the sacroiliac joints and spine. A large proportion of patients with AS carry the HLA-B27 allele, making it an important genetic risk factor. HLA-B27 is also associated with other seronegative spondyloarthropathies such as reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and enteropathic arthritis. Rheumatoid arthritis is associated more with HLA-DR4 and ACPA positivity, while SLE is associated with different genetic factors. Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease and has no significant HLA-B27 association.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HLA-B27 → Ankylosing spondylitis

  • Part of seronegative spondyloarthritis group

  • Other associations: Reactive arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, enteropathic arthritis

  • AS affects: Sacroiliac joints and spine

  • RA association: HLA-DR4, ACPA

Exam Pearl:
HLA-B27 is the classic genetic marker associated with a

Medicine 10.question: ৪৭) Degenerative change in spine is called.....?
Medicine 10.exp:
Spondylosis refers to degenerative changes of the spine, mainly due to age-related wear and tear affecting the intervertebral discs, vertebral bodies, and facet joints. It may lead to osteophyte formation, disc space narrowing, and stiffness or pain in the spine. Spondylitis refers to inflammation of the vertebrae, such as in ankylosing spondylitis. Spondyloarthropathies are a group of inflammatory rheumatic diseases involving the spine and sacroiliac joints. Spondylolysis refers to a defect or stress fracture in the pars interarticularis of the vertebra, commonly in the lumbar region.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Spondylosis → degenerative spinal changes

  • Spondylitis → inflammatory vertebral disease

  • Spondyloarthropathies → group of seronegative inflammatory arthritis

  • Spondylolysis → pars interarticularis defect

  • Osteophytes are common in degenerative spine disease

Exam Pearl:
Degeneration of the spine = Spondylosis; inflammation of the spine = Spondylitis.

Medicine 10.question: ৪৮) Classical triad of Reiter's syndrome excludes.....?
Medicine 10.exp:
The classical triad of Reiter’s syndrome (reactive arthritis) consists of urethritis, conjunctivitis, and arthritis. It is a form of seronegative spondyloarthritis that typically occurs after gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection, commonly associated with organisms such as Chlamydia trachomatis. Non-specific urethritis and conjunctivitis are components of the classic triad, while reactive arthritis itself represents the arthritis component. Psoriatic spondylitis is a separate seronegative spondyloarthropathy associated with psoriasis and is not included in Reiter’s syndrome.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Reiter’s syndrome triad:

    • Urethritis

    • Conjunctivitis

    • Reactive arthritis

  • Associated with HLA-B27

  • Part of seronegative spondyloarthritis group

  • Psoriatic arthritis is a separate entity

Exam Pearl:
Reiter’s syndrome = “Can’t see, can’t pee, can’t climb a tree” (conjunctivitis, urethritis, arthritis).

Medicine 10.question: ৪৯) Which crystal is found in gout?
Medicine 10.exp:
Gout is caused by deposition of monosodium urate (MSU) crystals in joints and soft tissues due to hyperuricemia. These crystals trigger an intense inflammatory response mediated by neutrophils, causing acute gouty arthritis. Under polarized light microscopy, MSU crystals appear as needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals. Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystals are associated with pseudogout, not gout. Calcium oxalate crystals may occur in renal failure, and calcium phosphate crystals are associated with other crystal deposition disorders.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gout crystal: Monosodium urate (MSU)

  • Shape: Needle-shaped

  • Birefringence: Strong negative birefringence

  • Pseudogout crystal: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD)

  • Common site of gout: First metatarsophalangeal joint (podagra)

Exam Pearl:
Gout = Monosodium urate crystals with negative birefringence.

Medicine 10.question: ৫০) Microangiopathic hemolysis is indicated by.....?
Medicine 10.exp:
Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA) occurs when red blood cells are mechanically damaged while passing through abnormal small blood vessels, leading to fragmentation of RBCs. The characteristic peripheral blood film finding is red cell fragments (schistocytes). These are commonly seen in conditions such as thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP), hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS), disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC), and mechanical heart valve hemolysis. Spherocytes are seen in hereditary spherocytosis and autoimmune hemolytic anemia, sickle cells in sickle cell disease, and hypersegmented neutrophils in megaloblastic anemia.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • MAHA → Schistocytes (RBC fragments)

  • Common causes: TTP, HUS, DIC, prosthetic heart valves

  • Associated findings: ↑ LDH, ↑ indirect bilirubin, ↓ haptoglobin

  • Spherocytes → hereditary spherocytosis/AIHA

  • Hypersegmented neutrophils → megaloblastic anemia

Exam Pearl:
Microangiopathic hemolysis = schistocytes (fragmented red blood cells) on peripheral blood film.
